title: Constraint validation for readonly doesn't correspond implementations

labels.name: needs tests
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires someone to write tests

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

> Constraint validation: If the [readonly](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#attr-input-readonly) attribute is specified on an [input](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#the-input-element) element, the element is [barred from constraint validation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#barred-from-constraint-validation).

The thing is that this constraint validation does not correspond to reality. The specification specifies it for any input elements.

And here's what I discovered:

For chrome, elements: `input`, `button`, `select`, [`form-associated custom elements`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#form-associated-custom-element) - when adding the `readonly` attribute, the `willValidate` getter changes to `false`.

For firefox, elements: `input`, [`form-associated custom elements`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#form-associated-custom-element) - when adding the `readonly` attribute, the `willValidate` getter changes to `false`  (the unspecified elements that were in chrome obviously didn't change the state of the `willValidate` getter).

That is, we see that there are inconsistencies between implementations<strike>, but not only do the implementations not correspond to each other, but none of the implementations corresponds to the specification</strike>.

It feels like the specification needs to be edited. But in which direction? Chrome or Firefox?
